'''Barry Martin Simon ''' (born 16 April 1946)  is an American [[mathematical physics#Mathematically rigorous physics|mathematical physicist]] and was the [[IBM]] professor of mathematics and [[theoretical physics]] at [[Caltech]],<ref>[http://www.math.caltech.edu/people/simon.html Caltech Math Faculty page]</ref> known for his prolific contributions in [[spectral theory]], [[functional analysis]], and [[Theory of relativity|nonrelativistic]] [[quantum mechanics]] (particularly [[Schrödinger operator]]s), including the connections to [[atomic, molecular, and optical physics|atomic and molecular physics]]. He has authored more than 400 publications on mathematics and physics.

His work has focused on broad areas of mathematical physics and [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] covering: [[quantum field theory]], [[statistical mechanics]], [[Brownian motion]], [[random matrix|random matrix theory]], general nonrelativistic quantum mechanics (including [[Many-body problem|N-body]] systems and [[resonance]]s), nonrelativistic quantum mechanics in [[electric field|electric]] and [[magnetic field]]s, the semi-classical limit, the [[Decomposition of spectrum (functional analysis)#Decomposition into absolutely continuous, singular continuous, and pure point|singular continuous spectrum]], random and [[ergodic theory|ergodic]] Schrödinger operators, [[orthogonal polynomials]], and non-[[selfadjoint]] spectral theory.<ref name="ams2016">{{cite journal |last1=Gesztesy |first1=Fritz |last2=Harrell |first2=Evans M. |author-link2= Evans Harrell |last3=Deift |first3=Percy A. |last4=Rosen |first4=Lon |last5=Fröhlich |first5=Jürg |last6=Reed |first6=Mike |title=From Mathematical Physics to Analysis: A Walk in Barry Simon's Mathematical Garden |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |date=1 August 2016 |volume=63 |issue=7 |pages=740–752 |doi=10.1090/noti1403|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Early life==
Barry Simon's mother was a school teacher, his father was an accountant. His ancestors were from [[Odesa]] and [[Grodno]]. His grandfather, whose original surname was Slopak, adopted the surname Simon after immigrating to the United States.<ref name="heritageproject">{{cite web |title=Barry Simon, Mathematical Physicist |url=https://heritageproject.caltech.edu/interviews-updates/barry-simon |website=Heritage Project |access-date=8 November 2023 |language=en |date=7 July 2022}}</ref> Simon attended [[James Madison High School (Brooklyn)|James Madison High School]] in [[Brooklyn]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vogel |first1=Mike |title=What is it about Brooklyn's James Madison High? |url=https://www.amny.com/opinion/columnists/mike-vogel/what-is-it-about-brooklyn-s-james-madison-high-1.10529505 |work=am New York |date=June 10, 2015 |quote=The school has selected honorees for its 2016 Wall of Distinction, former Madison alumni association president Richard Kossoff told me. They include food critic Arthur Schwartz, renowned physicist and mathematician Barry Simon, screenwriter Roger Schulman, who co-wrote "Shrek," and the late David "Sonny" Werblin, the NY Jets owner who brought Joe Namath to the team.}}</ref><ref name="nytimes1962">{{cite news |last1=Terte |first1=Robert H. |title=One Student Plus one Challenge Equals One Perfect Math Score |work=The New York Times |page=39}}</ref> Simon is an [[observant Jew]].<ref name="heritageproject"/>

==Career==
During his high school years, Simon started attending college courses for highly gifted pupils at [[Columbia University]]. In 1962, Simon won a [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]] mathematics competition. ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that in order to receive full credits for a faultless test result he had to make a submission with MAA. In this submission he proved that one of the problems posed in the test was ambiguous.<ref name="nytimes1962"/><ref name="ams2016"/>

In 1962, Simon entered [[Harvard]] with a stipend. He became a [[Putnam Fellow]] in 1965 at 19 years old.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web |title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=December 9, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312205244/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref> He received his AB in 1966 from [[Harvard College]] and his PhD in [[Physics]] at [[Princeton University]] in 1970, supervised by [[Arthur Strong Wightman]]. His dissertation dealt with ''Quantum mechanics for Hamiltonians defined as quadratic forms''.<ref name="ams2016"/>

Following his doctoral studies, Simon took a professorship at Princeton for several years, often working with colleague [[Elliott H. Lieb]] on the [[Thomas–Fermi model]] and [[Hartree–Fock method]] of [[atom]]s in addition to [[phase transition]]s and mentoring many of the same students as Lieb. He eventually was persuaded to take a post at [[Caltech]], from which he retired in the summer of 2016.<ref name="ams2016"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Clavin |first1=Whitney |title=Lifetime of Numbers: Q&A with Barry Simon |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/lifetime-numbers-qa-barry-simon-51679 |website=Caltech News |publisher=California Institute of Technology |date=August 10, 2016}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
*1974: Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Vancouver<ref>{{cite book|chapter=''Approximation of Feynman integrals and Markov fields by spin systems'' by Barry Simon|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (Vancouver, BC, 1974)|volume=2|year=1975|publisher=Canad. Math. Congress|location=Montreal|pages=399–402|mr=0441161}}</ref>
*1981: Elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1981&unit_id=&institution=Princeton+University}} (Search on year 1981 & institution Princeton University.)</ref>
*1990: Elected correspondent member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. BARRY SIMON |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/m/simon-barry |website=Austrian Academy of Sciences |publisher= |date=}}</ref>
*2005: Elected fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Barry Martin Simon Membership |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/barry-martin-simon |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |publisher= |date=3 October 2024}}</ref>
*2012: Elected fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]. Retrieved 2013-07-20.</ref>
*2012: Awarded the [[Henri Poincaré Prize]]<ref name="ams2016"/>
*2015: Awarded the [[Bolyai Prize]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[http://mta.hu/news_and_views/mta-international-bolyai-prize-goes-to-barry-simon-135978/''Bolyai Prize goes to Barry Simon''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222174649/http://mta.hu/news_and_views/mta-international-bolyai-prize-goes-to-barry-simon-135978 |date=2015-12-22 }} Communication by [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (mta.hu). Retrieved 12 April 2015</ref>
*2016: Awarded the [[Steele Prize]] for Lifetime achievements<ref name="ams2016"/>
*2018: [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/heineman.cfm|title=Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics|publisher= American Physical Society|accessdate= 7 September 2018}}</ref>
*2019: Elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Galvin |first1=Molly |title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and Foreign Associates; Historic Number of Women Elected to Its Membership |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430143122/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 30, 2019 |website=News from the National Academy of Sciences |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |date=April 30, 2019}}</ref>
